ei.title: Breaking Out of the Echo Chamber
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: Breaking Out of the Echo Chamber These days, everyone accesses the news through the Internet or social media, and often selectively takes the information that suits their tastes or beliefs. However, consistently encountering similar perspectives without considering alternative views can lead you to be trapped in an “echo chamber.” An echo chamber refers to an enclosed space where sound doesn’t leak out and returns as an echo. The term “echo chamber” is also used to describe any situation in which you only hear opinions you already agree with. This can distort your understanding of reality, and limit your ability to think critically and engage in meaningful debates. Worse still, an echo chamber may foster social division, making collaboration on common issues challenging. To avoid falling into this trap, you must actively seek diverse sources of information and engage with people who have different views. Always remember to check the information you receive, and keep an open mind when discussing new ideas. Even if you really want something to be true, it doesn’t always mean that it is true.

questions.passage: Breaking Out of the Echo Chamber These days, everyone accesses the news through the Internet or social media, and often (A)[selectively / randomly] takes the information that suits their tastes or beliefs. However, consistently encountering similar perspectives without considering alternative views can lead you to be trapped in an “echo chamber. ” An echo chamber refers to an enclosed space where sound doesn’t leak out and returns as an echo. The term “echo chamber” is also used to describe any situation in which you only hear opinions you already agree with. This can (B)[distort / clarify] your understanding of reality, and limit your ability to think critically and engage in meaningful debates. Worse still, an echo chamber may foster social division, making collaboration on common issues challenging. To avoid falling into this trap, you must actively seek (C)[diverse / identical] sources of information and engage with people who have different views. Always remember to check the information you receive, and keep an open mind when discussing new ideas.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① selectively(선택적으로)+distort(왜곡하다)+diverse(다양한) ← 정답
❌ ② randomly(무작위로)는 취향에 맞는 정보만 고르는 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ clarify(명확히 하다)는 이해를 왜곡한다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ identical(똑같은)은 다양한 출처를 찾으라는 문맥과 반대

❌ ② a fixed rule(고정된 규칙): 문맥에 맞지 않음
❌ ③ a busy schedule(바쁜 일정): 문맥에 맞지 않음
✅ ④ an open mind(열린 마음): 새로운 생각을 논할 때 열린 마음을 유지하라 ← 정답
det.tip: keep an open mind: 열린 마음을 유지하다

questions.passage: Breaking Out of the Echo Chamber These days, everyone accesses the news through the Internet or social media, and often selectively takes the information that suits their tastes or beliefs.  However, consistently encountering similar perspectives without considering alternative views can lead you to be trapped in an “echo chamber. ” An echo chamber refers to an enclosed space where sound doesn’t leak out and returns as an echo.  The term “echo chamber” is also used to describe any situation in which you only hear opinions you already agree with.  This can distort your understanding of reality, and limit your ability to think critically and engage in meaningful debates.  Worse still, an echo chamber may foster social division, making collaboration on common issues challenging.  To avoid falling into this trap, you must actively seek diverse sources of information and engage with people who have __________.  Always remember to check the information you receive, and keep an open mind when discussing new ideas.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① the same opinions(같은 의견): 반향실(에코 체임버)에 갇히는 원인이라 반대
✅ ② different views(다른 견해): 반향실을 피하려면 다른 견해를 가진 사람들과 소통해야 한다 ← 정답
❌ ③ no clear reason(뚜렷한 이유 없이): 문맥에 맞지 않음
❌ ④ fewer sources(더 적은 출처): 다양한 출처를 찾으라는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: engage with people who have different views: 다른 견해를 가진 사람들과 소통하다
